### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **5** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/plugin-audit`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **29** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**80** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83`.

⛔ **18** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **13** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **221** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **158** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **158**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **103** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **182** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `b59a30c2874734fc9b1c4e536b0a1348a3d70e10` — the merge of head `29c59f4d04e02b2953856d14c1bb46668715f371` into base `b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin b59a30c2874734fc9b1c4e536b0a1348a3d70e10 && git checkout b59a30c2874734fc9b1c4e536b0a1348a3d70e10
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83 29c59f4d04e02b2953856d14c1bb46668715f371 && git checkout -B drift-repro b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83 && git merge --no-ff 29c59f4d04e02b2953856d14c1bb46668715f371

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs b3098661cd3ad78634dd77a31ae68530ab9a3a83` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **Roster line (the schema face).** `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['platform-objects']` gains `'sys_lifecycle_state'` in sorted position between `'sys_jwks'` and `'sys_member'`; with it `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName` answer true for one more real object. A reference to that name now resolves instead of drawing the unknown-platform-name advisory; nothing accepted before is refused. **Right: widening, as declared.** Nothing else under `packages/spec` moves (file list and diff confirm: one hunk, one line). The roster test on `main` holds the roster to the declared `*.object.ts` set both ways, and the declaration is in this diff, so the pair is consistent.
2. **Same commit as the object.** Verified on the commit API, not the body: `04cab785` holds all 11 files (object, registration, index export, roster line, inventory row, census row, service, tests, changeset); `f9f4c1b6` touches only the changeset's `Skills-docs:` word. **Right**, per the consent's "same commit" term.
3. **The new object is what ruling B says.** `sys-lifecycle-state.object.ts`: `isSystem: true`, `managedBy: 'engine-owned'`, `systemFields: { tenant: false }` (ADR-0131 D7), `requiredPermissions: ['manage_platform_settings']`, `apiEnabled: false`, no `lifecycle` block, fields `id` / `last_swept_at` / `created_at` / `updated_at`; declared in `packages/platform-objects/src/system/` beside `sys-migration.object.ts` and registered in the same `PlatformObjectsPlugin` manifest (`[SysMigration, SysMigrationJournal, SysSecret, SysExchangeRate, SysTrustedKey, SysLifecycleState]`, no routing triple). Compared field-for-field with `sys_migration` on `main`: same posture. No settings key, no env override, no audit row, no Setup nav. **Right: engine-owned, tenant-less, beside sys_migration.**
4. **`@objectstack/platform-objects` public surface.** `SysLifecycleState` is exported from `system/index.ts`, which the package root re-exports with `export *`. One new named export; nothing removed. **Widening, covered by the minor.**
5. **`@objectstack/objectql` public surface.** `LifecycleEngineLike` (exported from the package root on `main`) gains three OPTIONAL members `findOne` / `insert` / `update`; an engine missing any keeps the old schedule. **Widening, as declared.** `LIFECYCLE_STATE_OBJECT` / `LIFECYCLE_STATE_ROW_ID` are module-level exports of `lifecycle-service.ts` and are NOT re-exported from `src/index.ts`, so they are not in the published accept set (the body's "new exported constants" overstates them; harmless).
6. **Sweep scheduling honours the watermark.** Read against the live engine on `main`:
   - `runFirstScheduledSweep`: fresh store (`wasDatastoreCreatedFromEmpty`, which on `main` requires zero existing tables and at least one created, so an UPGRADE boot onto an existing store that merely gains the new table is NOT fresh) ⇒ defer one interval and seed the row at now, no read. Otherwise one `findOne` by primary key under `SYSTEM_CTX`; young ⇒ no sweep, the read is the only statement; old, absent, unparsable, negative age (clock moved back), unregistered object, missing engine verbs, or a throwing read (warn once) ⇒ sweep at the initial delay, exactly as before. The interval is armed in `start()` either way. **Right.**
   - First boot / cold start on an existing store with no row: sweep, then insert. **Right.**
   - Multi-instance: two kernels on one store both read; a kernel that boots after another's completed sweep skips inside the interval; two that both find it old both sweep (idempotent reaps) and both write. A concurrent first boot of two kernels onto one empty store makes the second seed insert fail on the primary key: logged once at warn, presence reset to unknown, the next write re-reads. Degradation only. **Acceptable.**
   - Clock skew across instances: a future stamp reads as negative age ⇒ sweep; an ahead-clock instance reading a correct stamp sees it older ⇒ sweep. Both directions fail toward sweeping. **Right.**
   - Failed watermark write: never thrown, warn once then debug, presence reset; the next boot sweeps again (today's behaviour). **Right, and the ruling's "the row can only ever save work, never withhold it" holds.**
   - The write advances only a COMPLETED sweep: `audited && report.errors.length === 0 && !this.stopped`, stamped with `report.at` (the sweep's start, which the cutoffs were taken from). Early returns in `sweep()` (re-entrant, disabled, torn down, no engine, governance snapshot failed, governance disabled, leg-boundary stop) all precede the write. `auditReferences` now returns `true` when it ran or was never meant to, `false` on throw or teardown. **Right.**
   - Engine contract: `findOne(object, { where: { id }, context })`, `update(object, { id, last_swept_at }, { context })` (the engine extracts the id from `data`), `insert(object, row, { context })` — the same shapes `migration-flag.ts` uses on `main` for `sys_migration`; `isSystem: true` bypasses the static readonly strip (`engine-validate.ts`), so the `readonly: true, required: true` `last_swept_at` is written as `sys_migration.last_run_at` is. **Right.**
   - Direct `sweep()` always sweeps (one presence read on first write, documented); `OS_LIFECYCLE_DISABLED=1` arms nothing. **Right.**
7. **Nothing narrows.** No accepted input is refused; no default moves; the fresh-store deferral of #30214 is kept; a kernel without the object or the verbs behaves as on `main`.
8. **Census / inventory treatment of a tenant-less object.** Census row `reach: out`, `tenantField: null`, reason `systemFields.tenant: false`; totals 93→94, outOfReach 46→47, the reason bucket 20→21, inReach unchanged. Inventory row `census: PMAIN`, `fate: 'column-drop'`, citing `CENSUS_MAIN` and D7 — the same shape as `sys_trusted_key`'s row directly above it. `deployment-level-no-tenant-column.test.ts` adds the object to the D7 table (no injected or declared `organization_id`, opt-out via `systemFields.tenant`, platform-only capability). `check:platform-object-tenancy-census` ran in the green "Lint · repo & tooling gates". **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29918-lifecycle-sweep-watermark.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/platform-objects`, `@objectstack/cli`. No `major` (pre-GA rule of `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`). Level axis: `Metadata-protocol: added` requires at least one package whose published source moves at `minor` or above — spec and platform-objects both do; `added` sits beside `Clause-②: yes (widening)`, no contradiction. The **Check Changeset** run on this head concluded `success`.
- Declaration lines are identical in the PR body and the changeset: `Clause-②: yes (widening) — …`, `Metadata-protocol: added`, `Skills-docs: none — REASON`. `Fixes #29918` and `Fixes #30641` are both in the body. Every consent term of 6669304514 / 6670346930 is met.
- **`Skills-docs` spelling.** The declared grammar (pm-dispatch SKILL.md, the `Metadata-protocol` row) is `updated here | follow-up owed — FILES | follow-up #N | none — REASON`. `no move` (the order's and the release's word) is not in it. No script reads the line (the only `Skills-docs` hit under `scripts/` and `.github/` is a comment in `check-skills-token-ratchet.mjs`), so the gates are indifferent; the dev's `none — REASON` is the grammar the seat's ACCEPT checks against, and the reason given (no roster enumerated in `skills/**` or `content/docs/**`; no data API) matches the diff. **Right.**

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions: []`. The dev's four deviations and one acceptance note, each answered:

1. Squash of the released branch into one commit — verified (①.2); the released branch `claude/project-thread-0jjbbb@4a9c5296` compares to the same 11 files against `6ef7f583`, so the squash dropped nothing. The release note's "regenerated translation bundles" (6671108523) described files that were never on that branch; none are needed (see ④.4). **Accepted.**
2. `Skills-docs: none — REASON` instead of `no move` — the right grammar (②). **Accepted.**
3. `firstSweepDueAtInitialDelay` docblock reattached, no code moved — confirmed in the diff (the new methods sit above it). **Accepted.**
4. Assignee / reviewer not set (no MCP write) — the seat's stroke at hand-over. **Noted.**
5. Acceptance note: a fresh store now issues ONE write (the seed insert) at the initial delay, where the card's done-when says "at most the watermark read". The seed is card Expected item 2 ("seed the watermark when the tables are created") placed at the initial delay, one statement against the 130 measured, and it is what makes a reboot inside the first interval skip too. Ruling B's own done-when (a re-booted kernel with a young watermark issues only the read; an older one still sweeps) is met exactly. **Accepted as a declared deviation; the seat names it at ACCEPT and cloud re-measures under cloud#3413.**

Author note: PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`; no outside author.

### ④ Design judgment

1. **Roster line against its first consumer.** `platform-object-names.test.ts` on `main` scans every `*.object.ts` and asserts equality both ways per package; the declaration and the line land together, so the test is green only with both — the consent's reason for riding one PR holds in the tree. The inventory test (`organization-ownership-inventory.test.ts`, "a platform object without a row reds here, by name") is satisfied by the new inventory row. No generated spec artifact derives from the roster (nothing under `packages/spec/scripts`, `packages/spec/generated` or `scripts/` reads `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE`), so `check:generated` has nothing to drift. **Holds.**
2. **Object against the ruling and its first consumer.** The sole reader and writer is `LifecycleService`, which asks `registry.getObject` before any statement, so the object is never read where it is not registered. Single-row shape per the ruling of record (the keyed `id` column leaves room for a second clock without a schema change). No `lifecycle` block, so the row that records the sweep is never reaped by it. **Holds.**
3. **Pins are real.** Read against the gates they pin: the "younger watermark issues only the read" pin asserts `statements() === 1` and `deletes === 0`, which the read-gate ablation (`watermarkIsYoung` forced false) turns red by sweeping; the "failed policy or throwing audit leaves the row unchanged" pin asserts zero inserts/updates on both paths, which the write-gate ablation (`if (true)`) turns red. The dev reports both ablations 1 failed / 8 passed with restore proven against HEAD (`ba3f2b02`), and the first read-gate attempt refused as a no-op is recorded honestly. The remaining pins (no row ⇒ sweep + insert; fresh ⇒ seed without read, sweep one interval later; failing read ⇒ sweep + one warn; unregistered ⇒ never asked; direct sweep ⇒ sweeps and advances; disabled ⇒ zero statements) each name a distinct branch of `runFirstScheduledSweep` / `writeWatermark`. **Holds.**
4. **Dogfood cell and derived gates.** "Dogfood Regression Gate", "Governed Surface Queue Guard", "Check Changeset", "PR-body guards", "Lint · repo & tooling gates" (census check), "Lint · PM dispatch-gates", "Lint · ESLint", "Spec property liveness", "Type Check · source gates" all `success` on this head. Still `in_progress` at review time: Build Core, Test Core 1–8, Type Check · workspace / debt ledger / consumer gates (the last runs `check:i18n` and the coverage ratchet), Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · scoped slot lookup, the UI jobs. On `check:i18n`: `i18n-extract.config.ts` imports an explicit object list that already omits `sys_trusted_key` and `sys_migration_journal`, so the new object produces no bundle drift and is outside the ratchet's population; it has no UI (`apiEnabled: false`, no nav), so untranslated labels reach no user. The dev reports full dogfood 421 files / 3513 tests green under the verify lock and 94/94 derived gates exit 0. Landing precondition ② (every check green) is the dispatching seat's to confirm once the in-progress runs conclude; nothing read here predicts a red.
5. **Tried to break it.** Watermark older than the interval but a sweep aborted by `stop()` mid-leg: no write, next boot sweeps — correct. Row present with `last_swept_at` as a driver `Date` object: `String(date)` parses; as an epoch number it parses to NaN ⇒ sweep (conservative). `sweepIntervalMs` shortened between boots: compared against the new interval — correct. Governance `enabled: false` via settings: `sweep()` returns before the write, so the watermark does not advance while sweeping is switched off — correct (a later re-enable sweeps at once). A kernel that boots inside the interval repeatedly (cloud's 30-minute residency against the hourly interval): each boot reads one row and skips until the last completed sweep is an interval old, then sweeps at the initial delay — the "brief, frequent tenant is never swept" failure the card warned about does not occur. No must-fix found.

Should-fix (non-blocking, for the seat's ACCEPT note or a follow-up): (a) `system/index.ts`'s header docblock still lists what the module hosts without the new object — prose only; (b) the body's "new exported constants" are module exports, not package exports — wording only.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `29c59f4d04e02b2953856d14c1bb46668715f371`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/audit-writers.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/sys-lifecycle-state.object.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/system/index.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/plugin.test.ts, packages/platform-objects/src/deployment-level-no-tenant-column.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts, scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json, packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.ts, packages/objectql/src/lifecycle/lifecycle-service.test.ts (widened to the whole non-prose diff; the cited code on `main` — plugin-audit `read-audit.ts`, `parent-record-read-gate.ts`, `comment-access-hooks.ts`, `activity-changed-fields.ts`, `audit-hook-object-scope.test.ts`, `docs/adr/0057-system-data-lifecycle-and-retention.md` §3.3, `scripts/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs`, `.changeset/config.json` — was read, not reviewed)

Fresh record for the new head. The prior PASS 6673587300 named `f9f4c1b60342b2da2ab079f88d55b42f76943507` and does not carry; it is the baseline for everything the delta leaves alone. Governing text for the delta: file-surface amendment 6673909090, dev rework report 6674667474, ruling 6663872259 ("no audit row per sweep (not A)"), ADR-0057 §3.3 hard rule ("the LifecycleService's own deletes/rotations are not audited or activity-logged, otherwise cleanup re-feeds the tables it is draining"). Read-only shape held: `git diff f9f4c1b6 29c59f4d`, files via `git show`, both cards and the head's check-runs through the API. PR `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`.

**The delta.** One commit on top of `f9f4c1b6`, no merge of `main` (merge-base with `origin/main` is still `6ef7f583`, no merge commits on the branch). Three files, +33/−1: `audit-writers.ts` (one `SKIP_OBJECTS` entry with its comment), `audit-writers.test.ts` (one pin), the existing changeset (one frontmatter line, one sentence). Every other path of the PR is byte-identical to the reviewed head (`--stat` lists only those three), so baseline ① items 1, 2, 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8 hold at this head unchanged; item 3 is corrected below.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **`SKIP_OBJECTS` is the right seam, and the only one.** The CRUD ledger has ONE handler, `writeAudit`, registered on `afterInsert`, `afterUpdate` and `afterDelete` with `excludeObjects: AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` — a spread of the same set — and whose first line is `if (SKIP_OBJECTS.has(ctx.object)) return;`. One entry therefore unhooks all three verbs on both faces, registration and handler. There is no object-metadata opt-out: `enable.activities: false` drops only the `sys_activity` mirror and still writes the ledger row (test at line 815), and there is no "system-context writes are not audited" rule (the describe's own comment; the test at line 219 records a machine-originated write). The entry sits in group (2) beside `sys_job_queue` and `sys_upload_session`, whose posture it shares exactly: engine-owned, a single writer under `SYSTEM_CTX`, one or more writes per mechanical tick, no act anyone performed. The comment's claims were checked against the tree: `managedBy: 'engine-owned'` and `isSystem: true` on the object file, `LifecycleService` the sole reader and writer (baseline ①.6), one write per completed sweep. **Right.**
2. **Nothing else audits the row.** The other `sys_audit_log` writers in the tree are event-specific, not object hooks: `config-change-audit.ts` (settings keys), `admin-import-users.ts`, `action-invocation-audit.ts`, `auth-event-audit.ts`. The only other `sys_activity` hook, `installActivityStampHook` (`activity-changed-fields.ts`), is registered with `object: 'sys_activity'`. The wildcard `afterInsert` hooks outside plugin-audit (`auth-plugin.ts`, plugin-sharing `rule-hooks.ts` / `primary-bu-projection.ts`) write no ledger. So the ruling's "no audit row per sweep" now holds end-to-end, not only by declaration. **Right.**
3. **Correction to baseline ①.3.** At `f9f4c1b6` the object's "no audit row" was the declaration's intent, not the tree's behaviour: the generic writer audited the watermark insert, the aging sweep archived that ledger row, and Test Core 1/8 (the `cli` `audit-key-material` / `audit-mail-bodies` archive integration tests, case 4, archived 2 vs 1) caught it. The prior record read the declaration and not the writer; this head makes the declaration true. The archive tests' expected count is unchanged — the fix removes the spurious row rather than widening the expectation, which is the right direction.
4. **Derived consequences of the list entry, each intended.** `AUDIT_EXCLUDED_OBJECTS` has three other consumers on `main`: (a) `read-audit.ts` refuses a read-audit opt-in naming the object, with a warn, so the sweeper's one boot-time `findOne` is never read-audited either — consistent with the ruling and with `apiEnabled: false`; (b) `parent-record-read-gate.ts` drops it from the enumerated parents, and `commentThreadGate()` names every excluded object as a parent, so comment visibility is unchanged (and the object has no data API to be commented on); (c) `engine.ts` reads the registration face only. No business object changes posture: the control pins ("still audits ordinary business writes", `sys_file` stays audited) are untouched. **Nothing is unaudited by accident.**
5. **The pin is real.** The fake engine's `registerHook` ignores `excludeObjects`, so the handler fires for the object; past the skip line its only early return before the two `create` calls is `!api?.sudo`, which the fake supplies, and a `session: { isSystem: true }` write of a business object reaches the ledger (line 219). Deleting the entry writes a `sys_audit_log` and a `sys_activity` row for the insert and again for the update, `created` is non-empty, `toEqual([])` reds. The dev's ablation record agrees (delete of the line: 1 failed; restore blob equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` empty). The pin fires the two verbs the sweeper issues (insert, then update); delete is the same handler and is covered by the `sys_job_queue` lifecycle case beside it. **Holds.**
6. **Roster line (the schema face) unchanged.** `platform-object-names.ts` is identical to the reviewed head: one line, sorted between `sys_jwks` and `sys_member`, the roster test on `main` holds it to the declared `*.object.ts` set both ways. Widening as declared. **Holds.**
